description:
lightweight, open-source network monitor for Windows that displays live upload/download speeds directly on the Taskbar with a native look and feel.

A lightweight, open-source network monitor for Windows that displays live upload/download speeds directly on the Taskbar with a native look and feel.
✨ NetSpeedTray 2.2.0
Your history is now exact, the widget works with every Windows 11 taskbar position, and it uses much less memory. On 2.1.7 this one installs itself: click Download and it's done. After the update the app comes back as you, not as administrator.
Highlights
- Exact history, in a file about a quarter the size. The first launch converts your 2.1 history in seconds and keeps the old file as a backup.
- Every taskbar position. Top, left, right and the Small taskbar. Move or resize it and the widget follows, no restart. Thanks @un99known99.
- Much less memory. Roughly half of what 2.1.7 used, and Settings and the Monitor give their memory back when you close them.
- Out of the way of your apps. When your app buttons reach the widget it steps aside, and comes back when there's room. Thanks @relu616.
- A hover card with CPU, GPU, memory and battery, so the taskbar can show just your network speed. Thanks @kamal63442.
- Check connection tells you whether packet loss starts on your Wi-Fi or beyond it.
- Current LibreHardwareMonitor works for temperatures and power (turn on its Remote Web Server). Thanks @emgeka.
Top fixes
- The widget comes back on its own when the taskbar covers it. Thanks @kamal63442 and @pasharm.
- No more flashes over fullscreen videos and games. Thanks @kamal63442.
- The installed app is signed, so a clean install runs with Smart App Control on. Thanks @Keltian.
- A wrong PC clock can't wipe your history anymore.
- GPU usage matches Task Manager. Thanks @ivLis-Studio.
Heads up
- History totals read lower than 2.1.x showed. Nothing was lost: 2.1.x over-counted quiet minutes. Your data-cap figure doesn't change.
- Going back to 2.1.x shows your history but records nothing until you restore the backup. DATABASE.md has the steps.
- New defaults: the font (Segoe UI Variable, like the clock), the High/Medium/Low colors and the Trend mini graph. Colors and fonts you picked are kept.
There's a lot more, including multi-monitor fixes, data usage by day/month/year, Bengali and a reorganized Settings. It's all in the changelog.
Thanks
Code from @Zogar89, @ZeroFlagLabs, @pasharm, @kamal63442 and @emgeka, bug hunting and testing from @relu616, @Keltian, @kiro5678, @ivLis-Studio, @un99known99, @balciseri and @XYuki-cloud, and translations and reviews from @Askeleid, @cscsanaki, @boonstraworks, @lezgintekay, @doeil1614-ops and @RainThings. And thanks to everyone who ran the betas and release candidates.
Full changelog: https://github.com/erez-c137/NetSpeedTray/blob/main/changelog.md
